This problem arises whenever empirical practice offers several defensible covariance corrections. Cluster-robust procedures require a partition; factor corrections require a low-dimensional common component; and HAC, spatial, and network procedures require a bandwidth, distance, or adjacency rule (Liang and Zeger, 1986;Arellano, 1987;Newey and West, 1987;Andrews, 1991;Conley, 1999;Cameron et al., 2011;Auerbach, 2019;Leung, 2022). Existing methods explain how to conduct inference after a correction has been chosen. They provide less guidance about which scientifically credible restriction, if any, may safely be used for the particular coefficient or contrast under study. What the researcher does. The procedure is deliberately simple in concept. First, specify a finite collection of economically or institutionally motivated covariance restrictions and retain an unrestricted robust covariance estimator as a benchmark. Second, estimate the covariance operator that actually determines the asymptotic variance of the target contrast. Third, for each structured candidate, ask whether its omitted covariance matters for that contrast, rather than whether the entire covariance matrix is reproduced. Fourth, among numerically certified candidates, select the correction whose implied contrast variance is closest to the estimated unrestricted target variance; report the broad benchmark and the relevant diagnostics alongside it. This validity-efficiency trade-off is one of the paper's load-bearing theoretical results. A second asks how far the target-specific logic can be pushed across many contrasts. We derive a simultaneous contamination process over any prespecified compact family of loadings and prove a sharp converse: if a structured covariance approximation differs from the population covariance matrix, then some scalar contrast must be contaminated. Uniform exactness over all unit-norm contrasts is possible if and only if the covariance approximation is globally exact.

Why certification is separate. A candidate is certified when its numerical routine supplies a valid bound on optimization error relative to the stated covariance class. Certification means that the computer solved the approximation problem accurately; it does not mean that the covariance class is true or that the resulting confidence interval is valid. Statistical validity comes from operator matching plus class membership or contrast-local exactness. Keeping numerical certification, statistical validity, and adaptive selection distinct is essential, particularly for nonconvex covariance classes. Three deliverables for empirical practice. The framework has three deliberately distinct deliverables. It is efficient when valid : when a scientifically motivated structure is correct for the target and sufficiently separated, the feasible selector can inherit the structured estimator's efficiency gain. It is safe when detectable misspecification is present: the exactness diagnostic can trigger a prespecified fallback to unrestricted inference. And it is transparent when the data are inconclusive: contamination bands and coverage-risk envelopes quantify how much uncertainty remains when a non-rejection is weak evidence. These roles are complementary; a non-rejection is never treated as proof of validity. The empirical analysis mirrors these three deliverables. Fama-French calibrations show both a detector success-a High Technology shortening that the exactness test rejects and undercovers-and, under validity imposed by construction, a feasible selector that matches the oracle's 0.953 coverage and 39.2% RMSE gain. FHFA state house prices use externally fixed Census divisions to demonstrate target-specific verdicts in economically meaningful regional exposures, while the contamination-path experiment shows how coverage, rejection, and unrestricted fallback evolve as validity deteriorates. Cigarette demand supplies the complementary case in which unrestricted HAC remains primary. Real-data non-rejections are treated as permissive evidence and are paired with detectability and coverage-risk calculations.

The paper makes five contributions. First, it reframes covariance validity as a local, contrast-indexed restriction and derives a test with an explicit local power function. Second, it establishes a sharp growing-block efficiency-contamination frontier: valid structure can improve the convergence rate of the contrast-variance estimator, the block estimator attains a matching local asymptotic lower bound, and the rate gain survives a transparent weak temporal-dependence benchmark. Third, it develops simultaneous inference for contamination over prespecified families of contrasts and proves a no-uniform-free-lunch theorem: any genuinely misspecified covariance approximation must be wrong for at least one scalar contrast. Fourth, it turns candidate validity into adaptive inference through numerical certification, a margin-free oracle inequality, primitive coverage conditions, estimated-loading theory, a quantitative coverage-distortion bound, and a contamination-band coverage-risk envelope. Fifth, the applications make contrast specificity visible rather than rhetorical: the same covariance map is evaluated under different economic loadings, and realized precision is separated from demonstrated variance-estimation accuracy. Positioning. The framework differs from conventional dependence-robust inference because the correction itself is an object of disciplined choice for the inferential target. It differs from covariance-model selection because the objective is neither likelihood nor recovery of the full covariance architecture. It differs from model averaging (Claeskens and Hjort, 2008) because the baseline method selects among certified corrections and reports near-minimizers rather than averaging procedures. It also differs from generic post-selection inference: the main guarantee is not obtained by conditioning on a selected covariance model or by claiming uniform validity after discontinuous model selection (Leeb and Pötscher, 2005). The central object is the contrast contamination, and the guarantee is relative to the supplied candidate collection. A conventional robustness row can reveal that standard errors differ, but it provides no target-specific criterion for deciding whether a covariance restriction is harmless for the reported contrast. Here two candidate matrices with similar global fit can be ranked differently for two loadings q, and a fixed restriction can be formally rejected for one contrast while remaining admissible for another. That before/after distinction is the practical content absent from simply reporting several standard errors.

Scope. The baseline adaptive-inference theory is deliberately finite dimensional: N is fixed, T → ∞, the candidate collection is finite, and the formal fixed-map exact-ness theory covers one-way block corrections and other fixed linear maps such as the diagonal map. General support-selected sparse candidates are covered through the class-membership route unless additional selection-stability conditions are imposed. Factor approximations without a global numerical certificate remain diagnostics. The growing-block results are separate Gaussian triangular-array mechanism benchmarks in which the number of independently observed block contributions increases; when those contributions correspond to disjoint coordinates, the underlying dimension necessarily grows. They establish a sharp efficiency frontier for variance estimation, not a growing-dimensional validity theorem for the fixed-N adaptive selector. One permits a common finite-range serial correlation shape, but neither establishes general growing-dimensional validity of the full adaptive selector. Network, spatial, and semiparametric nuisance-learning extensions require additional theory and are not claimed here. The unrestricted robust correction is always reported because no adaptive procedure over a misspecified candidate collection can create validity from absent structure. The remainder of the paper follows the inferential pipeline. Section 2 defines the covariance approximation problem. Section 3 develops estimable approximation quantities. Section 4 develops contrast-local validity, its test, the efficiency benchmark, adaptive selection, and coverage. Section 5 discusses ambiguity and practical diagnostics. Section 6 studies finite-sample performance. Section 7 presents the Fama-French, FHFA house-price, and cigarette applications. Proofs, computation, additional simulations, and empirical sensitivity analyses appear in the Online Supplement.

This section develops the theory in four movements. First, contrast-local validity isolates the omitted covariance component that matters for the stated economic target, turns that restriction into a bootstrap test, and maps contamination confidence bands into Gaussian-reference coverage-risk envelopes. Second, finite-and growing-block results characterize what valid structure can buy: exact Rao-Blackwell improvement at fixed dimension and a sharp faster-rate efficiency frontier in a separate growingblock benchmark, with a matching local lower bound. Third, simultaneous-contrast and impossibility results show how far target-specific validity can be extended and why it cannot hold uniformly over all economic questions unless the covariance restriction is globally correct. Fourth, the oracle inequality and coverage theorem turn those ingredients into the paper's fixed-N adaptive decision rule. Global residuals and contrast-contamination diagnostics interpret the decision; they do not determine the formal action.

Use it when an externally defensible covariance restriction could stabilize a noisy unrestricted covariance estimate and the target-specific restriction can be examined directly. Do not expect it to help when unrestricted robust inference is already precise, every structured candidate is implausible for the contrast, or the main error comes from a poorly estimated long-run covariance. For an empirical application, the researcher can implement the method without learning a latent dependence label. First, define the scalar contrast and estimate the covariance matrix that governs its asymptotic variance. Second, specify a small dictionary of covariance restrictions from economic or institutional knowledge, not from the resulting p-values. Third, numerically certify each eligible approximation and, for fixed maps, report the estimated contrast contamination and its test. Fourth, compare the certified candidates by the contrastspecific variance discrepancy and report near-minimizers rather than forcing a sharp choice when the discrepancies are close. The Monte Carlo study evaluates the certified adaptive rule rather than recovery of a latent dependence label. Two additional experiments connect the main theory to the empirical implementation. Full results are in Online Supplement D. What the simulations establish. When the dictionary contains a good approximation, the certified adaptive rule can remain close to the realized oracle even without stable label recovery. Near ties make the selected label unstable before they make the inferential loss large, while global misspecification can invalidate every structured option. The simulations therefore support the paper's intended protocol: adapt only within a scientifically defensible collection, report decision sensitivity, and retain unrestricted inference whenever the operator estimate or the structured collection is doubtful.

The applications are organized around three empirical questions. Fama-French asks whether a canonical covariance restriction is credible for a specific portfolio contrast and whether the actual adaptive selector inherits the efficiency payoff predicted by the theory. An FHFA state-house-price application uses official public data and Census geography to show the method resolving economically meaningful regional exposure contrasts. Cigarette demand remains the complementary case in which unrestricted HAC is already competitive. A useful benchmark for reading the evidence follows directly from the efficiency theory. When a structured and an unrestricted estimator are both valid for the same contrast, they estimate the same population variance; the efficiency gain is lower sampling noise in that variance estimate, not a permanently smaller population standard error. Accordingly, the strongest positive evidence below is the closed-loop calibration showing coverage and variance-estimation RMSE for the actual selector. Real-data standard-error shortenings are reported as realized differences and are interpreted jointly with the exactness test, rather than as efficiency gains by themselves.

The resulting state-level slope estimates answer a simple economic question: how strongly does a state's housing market co-move with the national housing cycle? The structured candidate is fixed externally by the nine Census divisions (U.S. Census Bureau, 2021); diagonal covariance is the aggressive comparator. Table 2 reports the equal-state average and four prespecified region-versus-rest contrasts, holding the covariance map and Bartlett bandwidth four fixed. The economically strongest results are the regional exposure differences. Midwest states have an average national-cycle loading about 0.334 below the rest of the country; unrestricted and division-structured standard errors are 0.0578 and 0.0468, a 19.0% reduction. The pointwise exactness p-value is 0.208 and the simultaneous familywise value is 0.419. The FHFA application provides a structurally distinct case based on official public data, official Census geography, and genuinely non-uniform regional loadings. For the Midwest and West contrasts, the Census-division restriction is not rejected and the realized standard errors are 12-19% smaller. We do not treat non-rejection as proof of exactness. Online Supplement E therefore reports pointwise contamination confidence bands, the Gaussian-reference coverage-risk envelope from Corollary 1, and 80%power detectable-contamination thresholds. At T = 140 those bounds remain wide, so they do not certify a small coverage distortion for Midwest or West. In plain terms, the data are compatible with coverage errors large enough that the 12-19% realized standard-error reductions should be read as permissive rather than validated gains. The positive evidence for coverage-preserving efficiency comes from the closed-loop calibration, while the housing application demonstrates how one external covariance map receives different target-specific verdicts in economically interpretable data. Data provenance and sensitivity analyses are also in Online Supplement E. Complementary cigarette-demand case. The Online Supplement revisits the U.S. cigarette-demand panel of Baltagi (2006). There the adaptive rule does not improve the headline inference and unrestricted HAC remains the natural primary benchmark, illustrating that the framework is not designed to force a structured correction in every dataset. Taken together, the three applications show the method in three distinct roles. Fama-French shows both detector success and a closed-loop calibration in which the actual selector attains the oracle efficiency payoff with nominal coverage. FHFA house prices show a structurally different public-data setting in which Census geography is not rejected for economically meaningful Midwest and West exposure contrasts and delivers 12-19% shorter standard errors. Cigarette demand provides a setting in which unrestricted HAC is already competitive. The framework therefore does not promise shorter intervals; it provides a testable and reproducible way to decide whether scientifically motivated structure is credible for the variance of the economic target.

This paper develops contrast-local validity for inference when several dependence corrections are scientifically plausible. A covariance approximation can be globally wrong yet adequate for a specified economic contrast because only the omitted covariance that loads on that contrast affects its asymptotic variance. For fixed covariance maps this contamination is estimable and testable, with local-power theory, simultaneous inference over prespecified families of loadings, and a bootstrap confidence-band construction that can be translated into a Gaussian-reference coverage-risk envelope. The sharp converse is equally important: unless the covariance approximation is globally exact, some scalar contrast must be contaminated. Target specificity is therefore a mathematical necessity rather than a presentational choice. The efficiency theory describes what valid structure can buy and what it costs. With finitely many correct Gaussian blocks, the structured variance estimator is the exact Rao-Blackwell improvement, the unique UMVUE, and attains the Cramér-Rao bound. In the separate growing-block benchmark its error is of order V 0 H T /T rather than V 0 / √ T , with a matching local asymptotic minimax lower bound; under balanced contributions this becomes the √ T G T rate. A non-Gaussian long-run quadratic-noise decomposition identifies the same variance-reduction mechanism under independent weakly dependent blocks, while a common finite-range Gaussian temporal benchmark preserves the rate ratio. The price is exact: contamination must shrink on the same faster scale. Sharper structure creates more potential efficiency and simultaneously demands stricter target-specific validity.

The adaptive procedure supplies the feasible decision layer in the baseline fixed-N , finite-dictionary problem. Numerically certified candidates are ranked by their estimated contrast-specific variance discrepancy, producing a margin-free oracle inequality and first-order coverage under either class membership or contrast-local conditions. Numerical certification is deliberately separate from statistical validity: it verifies that an approximation problem was solved accurately, not that the corresponding covariance restriction is true. The unrestricted robust interval remains the prespecified benchmark whenever the operator estimate or the target-specific restriction is doubtful. The empirical evidence illustrates this division of labor. In Fama-French industries, the same FF5 map receives different verdicts for different loadings; a mechanically attractive High-Technology shortening is rejected and severely undercovers in calibration. Under FF5 exactness, however, the actual adaptive selector covers at 0.953 and achieves the same 39.2% variance-estimation RMSE reduction as the oracle structured estimator. A contamination-path experiment connects these endpoints: as misspecification increases, adaptive coverage deteriorates, exactness rejection rises, and a test-gated fallback restores coverage toward the unrestricted benchmark. In FHFA state house prices, externally fixed Census divisions are not rejected for Midwest and West national-cycle exposure contrasts but are rejected for the Northeast; power calculations also show why those non-rejections should not be mistaken for equivalence. Cigarette demand provides the complementary case in which unre-stricted HAC remains primary. The practical prescription has three parts: exploit structure when target-specific validity is credible, use the exactness diagnostic with an unrestricted fallback when harmful misspecification is detectable, and report a contamination or coverage-risk envelope when the data cannot sharply distinguish the two. Operationally, this means naming the economic contrast, estimating the covariance object that governs it, specifying a small externally defensible dictionary, certifying the numerical approximations, and quantifying target-specific contamination before relying on structured inference. The paper does not claim a general growing-dimensional adaptive theorem or distribution-free optimality for long-run variance estimation. Within its stated scope, it turns an often implicit choice of robust standard error into a testable, contrastindexed decision problem with a sharp efficiency frontier and a transparent fallback.

p.t: The first empirical application uses monthly value-weighted returns on the 49 Fama-French industry portfolios and the monthly market, SMB, HML, and risk-free series. The portfolio definitions follow SIC-based assignments. Months with a missing value for any of the 49 industries are removed so that every industry regression is estimated over the same T = 682 observations from 1969:07 through 2026:04. For each industry, OLS estimates the three-factor regression in equation ( 46). Let and s jt = (s j,1t , . . . , s j,N t ) ′ . For an equal-weight average coefficient q = N -1 1 N , the target asymptotic variance is q ′ Γ LR 0,j q, where Γ LR 0,j is the long-run covariance of s jt . We estimate it using the same Bartlett rule as in the cigarette application. Externally fixed design. The five-group block candidate coarsens the 49 industries into the canonical broad Fama-French categories Consumer, Manufacturing, High Technology, Health, and Other. This taxonomy is external to the covariance fit and is fixed before computing the adaptive ranking. We use "externally specified" rather than "preregistered": the taxonomy is fixed independently of the covariance fit, and no preregistration claim is made. The second formal candidate is diagonal, corresponding to the zeroedge sparse class. Both projections are exact and therefore numerically certified. The adaptive rule minimizes the estimated variance discrepancy; importantly, it does not select the candidate with the smallest standard error mechanically.
